advisories.summary: Zod can exhaust memory while validating oversized constrained collections
advisories.exposure: The CLI validates provider responses, manifests and local configuration with Zod. A hostile or malformed input could exhaust memory in the CLI process. Exploitability requires control of validated input; no remote code execution was demonstrated.
advisories.rationale: The consumer lock installs Zod 4.6.7, outside the affected range; the package range stays compatible with every dependent (^4.x).

advisories.summary: Electron: Mitigation for compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates
advisories.exposure: The Windows ZIP/Setup and Linux AppImage embed Electron 44.5.1. Exposure depends on a compromised certificate chain presented to the packaged browser runtime; no Babel-specific exploit was demonstrated.
advisories.rationale: Electron 44.5.1 is pinned in babel-desktop packaging scripts, both package locks and the release workflows. Moving to 44.9.1 requires a Desktop build plus Windows install/repair/upgrade qualification that this Linux-only lane cannot execute, so no Desktop artifact is qualified for promotion.
advisories.releaseImpact: Desktop artifacts (Windows ZIP, Setup.exe, Linux AppImage) stay unqualified and require an owner decision before publication. The release workflow records this deferred advisory and installed version in release-qualification.json; it does not block building or opening the draft, and an unavailable review outcome fails the draft gate. The npm tarball is unaffected because Electron is not a CLI dependency.
